CS attends talent event in Dongguan
body:
Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today attended an opening ceremony for two initiatives promoting the Greater Bay Area (GBA) in Dongguan – namely the fourth GBA High-quality Talent Development Conference and the third GBA Doctoral and Postdoctoral Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition.

 

Addressing the ceremony, he said Hong Kong will continue to attract the talent required for its own and the country's development, and will work with other GBA cities to advance the alignment of rules and mechanisms that  facilitate the flow of talent within the area.

 

Mr Chan outlined that Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proactively aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and promotes the integrated development of education, technology and talent. He added that the Northern Metropolis University Town will closely connect Hong Kong's strengths in basic research and internationalised education with both the innovation and technology (I&T) and talent resources of the broader GBA.

 

After the ceremony, Mr Chan and Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun toured the exhibition hall and visited the Hong Kong Talent Engage booth.

 

Yesterday, Mr Chan and his delegation visited a key I&T enterprise in Dongguan to better understand the local model of fostering co-operation between the spheres of scientific research, innovation, and talent development. They subsequently toured the City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) to learn about synergies between Hong Kong and Dongguan in higher education and talent cultivation, and to explore ways of strengthening complementarity between the two places.

 

Mr Chan and Mr Sun concluded their visit to Dongguan this morning and returned to Hong Kong in the afternoon.

title: Event showcases tech achievements
body:
The InnoCarnival 2026, showcasing local innovation and technology (I&T) achievements, kicked off today at the Hong Kong Science Park in Sha Tin.

 

Under the theme "Lead with I&T Dream to Fly High", the event also features an aerospace thematic zone presenting research projects from local universities and their contributions to the country's space exploration missions.

 

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said that Hong Kong's strong frontier research capabilities, comprehensive financial services and world-class international talent together provide a complete pathway for turning ideas into industries.

 

He stressed that Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, announced last month, positions the Northern Metropolis as a hub for I&T industries, promoting the integrated development of education, technology, talent and industry to closely align university talent development and research with industry needs. The Government will also leverage Hong Kong's financial strengths to channel more patient capital into supporting research teams and start-ups as they progress from research and development (R&D) to application.

 

Mr Chan said that I&T development ultimately depends on people, particularly the younger generation, adding that the InnoCarnival encourages public learning through exhibits, workshops, talks and interactive experiences.

 

Citing a mobile food-waste paper machine that took top prize in the junior secondary division of this year's Hong Kong Student Science Project Competition, Mr Chan urged young people to draw inspiration from everyday life and consider how to make the city a better place.

 

"The idea is not complicated, but with dedication to putting it into practice, even a small invention can make a big difference. The next invention to reach the world may well come from one of the students here today." he said.

 

The Carnival will run until November 1 for nine consecutive days. Admission is free. Click here for details.

title: FS welcomes 18 leading enterprises
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan welcomed a new batch of 18 strategic enterprises establishing or expanding their operations in Hong Kong during a signing ceremony held by the Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (OASES).

 

Mr Chan welcomed the new partners. He noted that half of the enterprises came from the Chinese Mainland, while the other half came from various parts of the world. Their businesses cover a wide range of sectors, from advanced manufacturing and new energy to artificial intelligence (AI), life and health technology, fintech, and cultural and creative technology. Several of the enterprises have market capitalisations or valuations exceeding $100 billion.

 

The total number of OASES enterprises has reached 142 with the addition of this new batch. Mr Chan said the enterprises are expected to bring in some $84 billion of investment and create about 27,000 jobs. Their total investment has exceeded expectations by 30%, while the jobs created rose by 34%, having taken up more than 2.8 million sq feet of commercial and industrial space.

 

“Yet these figures tell only part of the story. What matters is the difference these enterprises can make in driving our innovation and technology sector forward, providing new impetus to our economy and employment, as well as solutions that make people's lives better.” he said.  

 

He highlighted some examples of the new partners.

 

“One of the strategic enterprises in this batch has developed real-time AI-empowered risk scores to predict patient deterioration in general wards and intensive care units, allowing medical intervention to come much earlier.”

 

“Another strategic enterprise will deploy its AI+Smart vehicle technologies and Internet of Vehicles applications in Hong Kong to accelerate the wider adoption of EVs (electric vehicles), while using our city as a testing ground to advance green and smart mobility in the region. This is the kind of impact we would like to see. “

 

Director-General of OASES Peter Yan noted that these leading enterprises will not only bring capital, technology, and talent, but also serve as "chain leaders" to cluster upstream and downstream enterprises and partners in Hong Kong. These entreprises will foster deep integration across the industry, innovation, and capital chains, further consolidating Hong Kong's position as an I&T hub.

title: APEC ministers' meeting opens
body:
The two-day Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting 2026 opened in Hong Kong today, marking the first time the city has hosted the event.  

 

Aiming to strengthen regional economic and financial co-operation, participants are discussing the global and regional macroeconomic outlook, fiscal policies supporting households, digital infrastructure financing, financial inclusion and dialogue with financial talent.

 

Speaking at the opening ceremony this morning, Minister of Finance Lan Fo'an noted that a new wave of breakthroughs in technological innovation and industrial transformation is accelerating, gathering new development momentum. He added that as the engine of global economic growth, the Asia-Pacific region bears greater responsibility.

 

Mr Lan said all parties should firmly implement the consensus reached at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting to contribute to regional prosperity. He urged member economies to strengthen macroeconomic policy dialogue and maintain stability.

 

Given the highly uncertain international economic environment, he advised economies to enhance the soundness of their own policies while boosting communication and co-ordination to prevent negative spillover effects from policy adjustments. He also stressed the need to accelerate economic transformation and enhance resilience by seizing opportunities in digital and green transformation, promoting innovative co-operation in artificial intelligence, the digital economy and green and low-carbon development, and cultivating new growth drivers.

 

Furthermore, he noted that development must remain a priority to promote shared prosperity. Mr Lan urged all economies to deepen practical co-operation in fiscal and financial fields, foster an open regional economic environment, maintain stable supply chains, and advance regional economic integration.

 

Addressing the discussion sessions, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Hong Kong would leverage its unique advantages under the "one country, two systems" principle. He emphasised that the city will make full use of its diverse financing channels and professional services as an international financial centre to serve as a "super connector" and "super value-adder". 

 

He highlighted that by connecting capital, technology and projects across the region, Hong Kong will work with other economies to foster resilient, sustainable and inclusive growth.

 

Chief Executive John Lee officiated at a welcome dinner for delegates this evening. 

 

“Together, we seek to build economies that are more resilient, innovative and inclusive to create continuing opportunities for our businesses, communities and future generations,” he said. 

 

He noted that as a founding member of the World Trade Organization, Hong Kong champions free trade and maintains a zero-tariff policy, a simple and low tax regime, and a predictable business environment, contributing to the city's status as a global financial centre. Mr Lee reiterated the Government’s commitment to strengthening Hong Kong's roles as a global offshore renminbi business hub, an international asset and wealth management centre, and a risk management centre, while advancing commodity trading and green financial services.

 

The Chief Executive pointed out that the Northern Metropolis is fast becoming Hong Kong's new economic engine.

 

“The Northern Metropolis is connected to the enterprising and innovative Mainland city of Shenzhen, where the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting is set to take place next month. It will become an innovation and technology hub and home to three university towns, integrating education, technology and talent,” he said.

 

Mr Lee added that the Northern Metropolis will deepen collaboration within the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area – a cluster city development that brings together Hong Kong, Shenzhen and nine southern cities with a combined gross domestic product that rivals the world's 10th largest economy.
